description: The plot titled “Hidden State Mean” illustrates mean absolute hidden-state values across network layers for three conditions (before gating, after gating, and a baseline). The x-axis is labeled “Layer,” uses a linear scale, and spans approximately layers 0 to 23 with regularly spaced tick labels at 0, 5, 10, 15, and 20. The y-axis is labeled “Abs Mean,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from about 0 up to roughly 4.5 with tick labels at integer values (0, 1, 2, 3, 4). Three lines are shown: a blue dashed line (no markers) for “hidden state mean before gate, avg 0.71,” which starts near ~0.05 at layer 0, rises to around ~0.25 by about layer 2, stays in the approximate ~0.2–0.5 range through about layers 3–18, increases to roughly ~0.9 near layer 20, then jumps sharply to about ~2.6 at layer 21, remains near ~2.6 at layer 22, and ends around ~4.3 at layer 23; an orange dotted line (no markers) for “hidden state mean after gate, avg 0.05,” which stays close to 0 for early layers and gradually increases to small positive values (on the order of a few hundredths) through mid-to-late layers, reaching roughly ~0.1 near the final layers and ending around ~0.1 at layer 23; and a green solid line (no markers) for “hidden state mean of baseline, avg 0.04,” which similarly begins near 0 at layer 0 and increases gradually across layers to around ~0.1 by the final layer, ending near ~0.1 at layer 23.
